title: What will Donald Trump say during Midterm Rally in Wichita, Kansas originally scheduled for October 19, 2026? Deport / Deported / Deportation
rules:
If 
 Donald Trump says Deport / Deported / Deportation as part of Midterm Rally in Wichita, Kansas originally scheduled for October 19, 2026
, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
How this is resolved
Video of the Midterm Rally in Wichita, Kansas originally scheduled for October 19, 2026 using the live broadcast or stream.
If a consensus by Kalshi employees cannot be reached using video, internal & external (official) transcripts of the Midterm Rally in Wichita, Kansas originally scheduled for October 19, 2026 will be used.

Payout Criteria
The exact phrase/word, or a plural or possessive form of the phrase/word. 
Plural nouns occurring within proper nouns and noun phrases (e.g. names, titles, etc).
Donald Trump speaking in an official capacity.
For phrases with slashes like "Doge/Dogecoin," either word satisfies the criterion.

Doesn't count for payout
Grammatical/tense inflections are otherwise not included. 
Presence alone during a livestream is not sufficient for the market to qualify (e.g., inaudible private conversations on camera, unofficial statements picked up on a hot mic).
Except as otherwise specified, previously aired content, archival footage, and recordings captured at times, places, or events wholly separate from the featured address.

Payout for cancellations and delays
If an event is definitively cancelled or the event fails to qualify under the Payout Criterion, or any other circumstance prevents normal resolution, then the market for "Event does not qualify" resolves to Yes and all other markets will resolve to No.  
If the event is postponed, and such a postponement is announced by the end of the following calendar day to be rescheduled to a time within 14 calendar days, the markets shall remain open.

blind.reasoning: The Monday October 19 rally for Sen. Roger Marshall was confirmed at a Park City (Wichita-area) arena, with Trump due to speak at 6 p.m. during a nationwide midterm tour. Immigration is a near-constant theme in his rally speeches, and these usually run more than an hour, so saying 'deport', 'deported' or 'deportation' at least once is more likely than not. However, he often uses other phrasings like 'illegal aliens' or 'getting them out', and tense forms like 'deporting' don't count. I couldn't confirm what he actually said.
blind.falsifier: A full transcript of the Park City/Wichita rally shows Trump discussing immigration only with terms like 'illegal aliens,' 'removed,' or 'deporting' and never saying 'deport,' 'deported,' or 'deportation'; or the rally is cancelled.

final.reasoning: The low price suggests recent Trump rallies rarely include the exact words deport, deported or deportation, so I lowered my estimate a lot. It stays above 0.25 because immigration is a staple of his long rally speeches.
